official_questions.stem: The functional unit in Ecology is the
official_questions.core_fact: The ecosystem (Tansley 1935) is the basic structural and functional unit of ecology.

statements.t: The functional unit in Ecology is the population.

statements.t: The functional unit in Ecology is the ecosystem.

official_questions.rule: Ecosystem = functional unit (Tansley); species = basic unit of classification.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of an Ecotone
official_questions.core_fact: An ecotone is a transition zone between two ecosystems (e.g. river bank, mangrove, marsh/estuary, forest-grassland edge); a teak forest is a single uniform ecosystem.

statements.t: River Bank is an example of an ecotone.
Teak Forest is an example of an ecotone.
statements.fact: A teak forest is a single ecosystem, not an ecotone.

statements.t: Mangroves is an example of an ecotone.
Marshland is an example of an ecotone.

official_questions.rule: Ecotone = transition zone (edge effect); examples: estuary, mangrove, marsh, river bank, grassland-forest edge.

official_questions.stem: Coral Bleaching is associated with removal of
official_questions.core_fact: Coral bleaching is the expulsion of symbiotic zooxanthellae (dinoflagellate algae) from coral tissue under heat or other stress.

statements.t: Coral bleaching is associated with removal of Zooxanthellae.
Coral bleaching is associated with removal of Azotobacter.
statements.fact: Azotobacter is a soil nitrogen fixer.

statements.t: Coral bleaching is associated with removal of Paenibacillus.
statements.fact: Paenibacillus is a soil bacterium.

statements.t: Coral bleaching is associated with removal of Rhizobia.
statements.fact: Rhizobia are root-nodule symbionts of legumes, not of corals.

official_questions.rule: Bleaching: loss of zooxanthellae; driven by heat (>1 deg C above summer max), acidification.

official_questions.stem: A leaf of a tree adapted to a warm dry climate is:

statements.t: A leaf adapted to a warm dry climate is Large and thick.

statements.t: A leaf adapted to a warm dry climate is Small and thick.
A leaf adapted to a warm dry climate is Small and thin.
statements.fact: Dry-climate leaves are small and thick.

official_questions.rule: Xerophyte leaf: small, thick, waxy, sunken stomata; hydrophyte/rainforest: large, thin.

official_questions.stem: Biodiversity Hotspots are characterized on the basis of:
options: Endemic flowering plant and threat perception
official_questions.key: Endemic flowering plant and threat perception
official_questions.core_fact: Myers/Conservation International criteria: at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species (>0.5% of world total) AND loss of at least 70% of original habitat (threat).

statements.t: Biodiversity hotspots are characterised on the basis of Endemic flowering plant and threat perception.
statements.d: Endemic flowering plant and threat perception

statements.t: Biodiversity hotspots are characterised on the basis of Species of flowering plants.
statements.fact: Criteria: endemic plants + threat (habitat loss).

statements.t: Biodiversity hotspots are characterised on the basis of Endemic flowering plant.
statements.fact: Endemism must be combined with threat (>=70% habitat lost).

statements.t: Biodiversity hotspots are characterised on the basis of Diversity of plants.
statements.fact: Criteria are endemism + threat, not diversity alone.

official_questions.rule: Hotspot: >=1,500 endemic vascular plants + >=70% habitat lost; India has 4 (Himalaya, Indo-Burma, W Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland).

official_questions.stem: In which type of community, the number of species per unit area will be more
official_questions.core_fact: Species richness per unit area is highest in tropical rain forests and decreases towards the poles (latitudinal gradient).

The number of species per unit area is more in Taiga forest.
statements.fact: Taiga has low richness.

official_questions.rule: Diversity decreases from equator to poles; Amazon richest.

official_questions.stem: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) is also known as
official_questions.core_fact: CITES was signed in Washington DC on 3 March 1973 (in force 1975), hence 'Washington Convention'; India joined 1976; 3 March = World Wildlife Day.

official_questions.stem:
Statement A : Natality refers to the birth of individuals in a population.
Statement B : Natality rate is expressed as the number of individuals produced per female per unit time.
options: Both statements A and B are true
Both statements A and B are false
Statement A is true, but statement B is false
Statement A is false, but statement B is true
official_questions.key: Both statements A and B are true
official_questions.core_fact: Natality = births added to a population; natality rate is expressed per unit time, often as offspring per female (per capita) per unit time.

statements.t: Natality refers to the birth of individuals in a population.
Natality rate is expressed as the number of individuals produced per female per unit time.

official_questions.rule: Natality/mortality/immigration/emigration change N; rates are per capita per time.

official_questions.stem: Population density is generally expressed as
options: The total number of individuals in a population
The number of individuals per unit area
The geographic distribution of the population
The number of individuals within a sample area
official_questions.key: The number of individuals per unit area
official_questions.core_fact: Population density = number of individuals per unit area (or volume); total number = population size.

statements.t: Population density is expressed as the total number of individuals in a population.
statements.fact: That is population size; density is per unit area.

statements.t: Population density is expressed as the number of individuals per unit area.
Population density is expressed as the geographic distribution of the population.
statements.fact: Distribution/dispersion differs from density.

statements.t: Population density is expressed as the number of individuals within a sample area.
statements.fact: A raw count is not density unless divided by area.

official_questions.rule: Density = N per unit area/volume; size = N.

official_questions.stem: Choose the correct statement.
options: Producers in an aquatic ecosystem are green plants
Archea are a type of producers who use energy from chemical compounds
Consumers are heterotrophs able to produce their food
The stability of ecosystem depends on consumers
official_questions.key: Archea are a type of producers who use energy from chemical compounds
official_questions.core_fact: Producers are autotrophs: photoautotrophs (plants, phytoplankton) and chemoautotrophs (some archaea/bacteria using chemical energy). Consumers are heterotrophs that cannot make their food. In water the main producers are phytoplankton.

statements.t: Producers in an aquatic ecosystem are green plants.
statements.fact: Main aquatic producers are phytoplankton (algae), not green plants.

statements.t: Archaea are a type of producers who use energy from chemical compounds.
Consumers are heterotrophs able to produce their food.
statements.fact: Consumers cannot produce their own food.

statements.t: The stability of an ecosystem depends on consumers.
statements.fact: Stability depends chiefly on producers and biodiversity, not on consumers.

official_questions.rule: Producers = photo- + chemo-autotrophs; aquatic = phytoplankton.

official_questions.stem: Forests that are located in mid latitude areas between tropics and polar region
official_questions.core_fact: Temperate deciduous forests occupy mid-latitudes (about 30-50 N/S) between tropics and polar regions; coniferous (boreal/taiga) lie at higher latitudes (50-70 N).

statements.t: Temperate deciduous forests are located in mid-latitude areas between the tropics and the polar regions.
Coniferous forests are located in mid-latitude areas between the tropics and the polar regions.
statements.fact: Coniferous (taiga) forests lie at high latitudes (50-70 N).

statements.t: Grasslands are the forests located in mid-latitude areas between the tropics and the polar regions.
statements.fact: Grasslands are not forests (temperate grasslands exist but are non-forest).

statements.t: Scrub jungles are located in mid-latitude areas between the tropics and the polar regions.
statements.fact: Scrub jungles are dry tropical vegetation.

official_questions.rule: Tropics -> evergreen/deciduous; mid-latitudes -> temperate deciduous; high -> coniferous; polar -> tundra.

official_questions.stem:
Assertion (A) : Grazing food chain begins with dead leaves via herbivores to carnivores.
Reason (R) : In grazing food chain autotrophs capture energy and transfer to herbivores.
options: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
official_questions.key: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
official_questions.core_fact: Grazing food chain starts with living green plants (autotrophs) -> herbivores -> carnivores; detritus food chain starts with dead organic matter (dead leaves) -> decomposers.

statements.t: Grazing food chain begins with dead leaves via herbivores to carnivores.
statements.fact: Grazing food chain begins with living producers; dead leaves start the detritus food chain.

statements.t: In grazing food chain autotrophs capture energy and transfer to herbivores.

official_questions.rule: GFC: plants->herbivore; DFC: detritus->detritivore; in forests DFC carries more energy.

official_questions.stem: Biogeochemical cycle in which the main reservoir is not the soil
official_questions.core_fact: Gaseous cycles (N, C, O) have atmospheric/oceanic reservoirs; sedimentary cycles (P, S, Ca) have reservoirs in rocks/sediments (lithosphere). The nitrogen cycle's main reservoir is the atmosphere (78% N2).

statements.t: The sulphur cycle is a biogeochemical cycle whose main reservoir is not the soil.
The nitrogen cycle is a biogeochemical cycle whose main reservoir is not the soil.
statements.fact: Per the key this is not the answer; factually the nitrogen cycle's main reservoir is the atmosphere, so the statement is true.

statements.t: The phosphorus cycle is a biogeochemical cycle whose main reservoir is not the soil.
statements.fact: Phosphorus is stored in rocks/sediments and soil.

statements.t: The calcium cycle is a biogeochemical cycle whose main reservoir is not the soil.
statements.fact: Calcium is stored in rocks/soil.

official_questions.rule: Gaseous: N, O, C (atmosphere/ocean); sedimentary: P, S, Ca (lithosphere).
official_questions.key_note: Doubtful key: the nitrogen cycle is the classic cycle whose main reservoir is the atmosphere, not soil; sulphur is usually a sedimentary cycle. Key (sulphur) kept.

official_questions.stem: CR in IUCN red list refers to

statements.t: CR in the IUCN Red List refers to Endangered.
statements.fact: Endangered = EN.

statements.t: CR in the IUCN Red List refers to Critically endangered.

official_questions.rule: Threatened = CR, EN, VU; EW and EX are above them.
